1	package aider
2	
3	import (
4		"encoding/json"
5		"fmt"
6		"os"
7		"path/filepath"

9		"time"

11		"github.com/entireio/external-agents/agents/entire-agent-aider/internal/protocol"
12	)
13	
14	// Managed-block markers inside .aider.conf.yml. Everything between them is
15	// ours to rewrite or remove; everything outside is the user's and is never
16	// touched.
17	const (
18		markerBegin = "# >>> entire-agent-aider (managed) >>>"
19		markerEnd   = "# <<< entire-agent-aider (managed) <<<"
20	)
21	
22	// notificationCommand is what aider runs through a shell when a model round
23	// finishes.
24	//
25	// The `echo {}` is load-bearing, not decoration. Aider invokes this with
26	// subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True) and passes no stdin of its own (io.py:1094),
27	// but Entire's external-agent bridge reads the hook payload from stdin before
28	// it ever reaches this plugin and rejects an empty read with
29	// "parse-hook: read stdin: empty hook input". That surfaces to the user as
30	// "Failed to run notifications command: ..." on every single turn. Feeding it
31	// an empty JSON object satisfies the bridge; this plugin ignores the payload
32	// and derives everything from the transcript, because aider has nothing to put
33	// in it.
34	//
35	// `echo {} | ...` is valid in both POSIX sh and cmd.exe, and needs no path
36	// quoting, so it works wherever aider runs. The command names the `entire`
37	// binary resolved through PATH — never a path inside the working tree, since
38	// this file is commonly committed.
39	const notificationCommand = "echo {} | entire hooks aider " + HookNameTurnEnd
40	
41	// managedBlock is the configuration install-hooks writes.
42	//
43	// Every key here is a normal aider long option. aider parses .aider.conf.yml
44	// with configargparse and includes the git-root copy in default_config_files
45	// (main.py:474-475), so a plain `aider` run in this repo picks all of it up
46	// with no wrapper and no shell involvement.
47	//
48	// `notifications: true` is not optional. IO.ring_bell guards on
49	// `self.bell_on_next_input and self.notifications` (io.py:1090), so setting
50	// only notifications-command is a silent no-op that captures nothing.
51	//
52	// The command names the `entire` binary resolved through PATH, never a path
53	// inside the working tree: this file is committed in many repos, and a
54	// repo-relative command would run whatever the checked-out branch contained on
55	// every aider turn.
56	func managedBlock() string {
57		return strings.Join([]string{
58			markerBegin,
59			"# Managed by Entire. Edit above or below this block, not inside it.",
60			"# Remove with: entire-agent-aider uninstall-hooks",
61			"notifications: true",
62			`notifications-command: "` + notificationCommand + `"`,
63			"chat-history-file: " + transcriptRel,
64			"llm-history-file: " + llmHistoryRel,
65			"input-history-file: " + inputHistRel,
66			markerEnd,
67		}, "\n")
68	}
69	
70	func (a *Agent) configPath() string {
71		return filepath.Join(protocol.RepoRoot(), aiderConfigFile)
72	}
73	
74	// InstallHooks writes the managed block into .aider.conf.yml.
75	//
76	// localDev is accepted and ignored: the protocol removed it because it asked
77	// agents to point hooks at a build inside the working tree.
78	func (a *Agent) InstallHooks(_ bool, force bool) (int, error) {
79		path := a.configPath()
80		block := managedBlock()
81	
82		existing, err := os.ReadFile(path)
83		switch {
84		case os.IsNotExist(err):
85			if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(block+"\n"), 0o600); err != nil {
86				return 0, fmt.Errorf("write %s: %w", aiderConfigFile, err)
87			}
88			return 1, nil
89		case err != nil:
90			return 0, fmt.Errorf("read %s: %w", aiderConfigFile, err)
91		}
92	
93		content := string(existing)
94		if hasManagedBlock(content) {
95			if !force && strings.Contains(content, block) {
96				// Already current; nothing to rewrite.
97				return 1, nil
98			}
99			content = replaceManagedBlock(content, block)
100		} else {
101			if !strings.HasSuffix(content, "\n") && content != "" {
102				content += "\n"
103			}
104			content += block + "\n"
105		}
106		if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(content), 0o600); err != nil {
107			return 0, fmt.Errorf("write %s: %w", aiderConfigFile, err)
108		}
109		return 1, nil
110	}
111	
112	// UninstallHooks removes the managed block, and the file if nothing else is
113	// left in it.
114	//
115	// Only this binary can remove its own hooks, so `entire disable --uninstall`
116	// cannot finish without it; a missing file is success, not an error.
117	func (a *Agent) UninstallHooks() error {
118		path := a.configPath()
119		existing, err := os.ReadFile(path)
120		if os.IsNotExist(err) {
121			return nil
122		}
123		if err != nil {
124			return fmt.Errorf("read %s: %w", aiderConfigFile, err)
125		}
126		content := replaceManagedBlock(string(existing), "")
127		if strings.TrimSpace(content) == "" {
128			// The file existed only to hold our block.
129			if err := os.Remove(path); err != nil && !os.IsNotExist(err) {
130				return fmt.Errorf("remove %s: %w", aiderConfigFile, err)
131			}
132			return nil
133		}
134		if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(content), 0o600); err != nil {
135			return fmt.Errorf("write %s: %w", aiderConfigFile, err)
136		}
137		return nil
138	}
139	
140	// AreHooksInstalled reports whether the managed block is present.
141	func (a *Agent) AreHooksInstalled() bool {
142		data, err := os.ReadFile(a.configPath())
143		if err != nil {
144			return false
145		}
146		return hasManagedBlock(string(data))
147	}
148	
149	func hasManagedBlock(content string) bool {
150		return strings.Contains(content, markerBegin) && strings.Contains(content, markerEnd)
151	}
152	
153	// replaceManagedBlock swaps the managed region for replacement, dropping it
154	// entirely when replacement is empty. Content outside the markers is preserved
155	// byte-for-byte.
156	func replaceManagedBlock(content, replacement string) string {
157		start := strings.Index(content, markerBegin)
158		if start < 0 {
159			return content
160		}
161		endIdx := strings.Index(content[start:], markerEnd)
162		if endIdx < 0 {
163			return content
164		}
165		end := start + endIdx + len(markerEnd)
166		// Absorb one trailing newline so removal does not leave a blank line.
167		if end < len(content) && content[end] == '\n' {
168			end++
169		}
170		if replacement == "" {
171			return content[:start] + content[end:]
172		}
173		return content[:start] + replacement + "\n" + content[end:]
174	}
175	
176	// --- parse-hook -----------------------------------------------------------
177	
178	// ParseHook translates an aider signal into a lifecycle event.
179	//
180	// turn-end is the only verb aider actually fires, and it arrives with an EMPTY
181	// payload: aider runs the notification command through a shell with no argv, no
182	// environment of its own and no stdin (io.py:1094). Everything is therefore
183	// derived from the transcript on disk.
184	func (a *Agent) ParseHook(hookName string, input []byte) (*protocol.EventJSON, error) {
185		switch hookName {
186		case HookNameTurnEnd:
187			return a.parseTurnEnd(), nil
188		case HookNameSessionStart:
189			return a.sessionEvent(input, eventSessionStart), nil
190		case HookNameSessionEnd:
191			return a.sessionEvent(input, eventSessionEnd), nil
192		default:
193			return nil, nil
194		}
195	}
196	
197	// sessionEvent builds a session lifecycle event from whatever payload arrived.
198	func (a *Agent) sessionEvent(input []byte, eventType int) *protocol.EventJSON {
199		ref := a.transcriptPath()
200		var hookInput protocol.HookInputJSON
201		if len(input) > 0 {
202			_ = json.Unmarshal(input, &hookInput)
203		}
204		if hookInput.SessionRef != "" {
205			ref = hookInput.SessionRef
206		}
207		sessionID := hookInput.SessionID
208		if sessionID == "" {
209			if data, err := os.ReadFile(ref); err == nil {
210				sessionID = sessionIDFromBanner(data)
211			}
212		}
213		if sessionID == "" {
214			return nil
215		}
216		return &protocol.EventJSON{
217			Type:       eventType,
218			SessionID:  sessionID,
219			SessionRef: ref,
220			Timestamp:  time.Now().UTC().Format(time.RFC3339),
221		}
222	}
223	
224	// parseTurnEnd decides whether the transcript actually advanced, returning nil
225	// when it did not.
226	//
227	// This never returns an error, on purpose. aider reports a non-zero exit from
228	// the notification command to the user as
229	// "Failed to run notifications command: ..." (io.py:1097), so any error here
230	// would print a warning into the user's session on every affected turn. An
231	// uninterpretable turn-end is reported as "nothing happened", which is what the
232	// protocol's null response already means.
233	func (a *Agent) parseTurnEnd() *protocol.EventJSON {
234		ref := a.transcriptPath()
235		data, err := os.ReadFile(ref)
236		if err != nil {
237			return nil
238		}
239		turns := parseTurns(data)
240		fp, ok := fingerprintOf(turns)
241		if !ok {
242			// The bell can ring before the user has submitted anything.
243			return nil
244		}
245	
246		// Require evidence that a model round completed. A confirmation prompt
247		// raised before any response — "Add foo.go to the chat?" during file
248		// mention detection — rings the bell with neither a usage report nor an
249		// applied edit recorded, and must not produce a checkpoint.
250		if fp.ReportCount == 0 && fp.EditCount == 0 {
251			return nil
252		}
253	
254		sessionDir := filepath.Dir(ref)
255		st := loadState(sessionDir)
256		if !fp.advancedOver(st.LastTurnEnd) {
257			return nil
258		}
259	
260		sessionID := sessionIDFromBanner(data)
261		if sessionID == "" {
262			return nil
263		}
264	
265		st.LastTurnEnd = fp
266		st.SessionID = sessionID
267		// A failure to persist costs at most one redundant checkpoint next time;
268		// failing the hook would cost the user a warning every turn.
269		_ = saveState(sessionDir, st)
270	
271		return &protocol.EventJSON{
272			Type:       eventTurnEnd,
273			SessionID:  sessionID,
274			SessionRef: ref,
275			Timestamp:  time.Now().UTC().Format(time.RFC3339),
276		}
277	}

1	package aider
2	
3	import (
4		"encoding/json"
5		"fmt"
6		"os"
7		"path/filepath"
8	)
9	
10	// turnFingerprint identifies how far a session has progressed.
11	//
12	// A plain turn index cannot decide whether a turn ended, because aider's
13	// notification is not a turn-end signal. IO.ring_bell fires at the first
14	// interactive prompt after IO.llm_started, and Coder.send_message reaches those
15	// prompts in this order:
16	//
17	//	base_coder.py:1423  llm_started()        -> arms the bell
18	//	base_coder.py:1531  show_usage_report()  -> writes "> Tokens: ..."
19	//	base_coder.py:1585  apply_updates()      -> writes "> Applied edit to ..."
20	//	base_coder.py:1589  auto_commit()        -> git commit
21	//
22	// A confirmation prompt inside apply_updates therefore rings the bell after the
23	// usage report but BEFORE the commit, while a turn needing no confirmation
24	// rings it at get_input() after everything. One turn can also produce several
25	// usage reports when a lint or test reflection loop runs.
26	//
27	// Comparing the whole fingerprint means a later firing that observes genuinely
28	// more work — another API call, another applied edit — counts as progress,
29	// while one that observes nothing new is dropped.
30	type turnFingerprint struct {
31		TurnIndex   int `json:"turn_index"`
32		ReportCount int `json:"report_count"`
33		EditCount   int `json:"edit_count"`
34	}
35	
36	func (f turnFingerprint) advancedOver(prev turnFingerprint) bool {
37		if f.TurnIndex != prev.TurnIndex {
38			return f.TurnIndex > prev.TurnIndex
39		}
40		return f.ReportCount > prev.ReportCount || f.EditCount > prev.EditCount
41	}
42	
43	// sessionState is the dedup bookkeeping, kept on disk because each turn-end
44	// runs in a fresh process that aider spawned.
45	type sessionState struct {
46		SessionID   string          `json:"session_id"`
47		LastTurnEnd turnFingerprint `json:"last_turn_end"`
48	}
49	
50	func statePath(sessionDir string) string {
51		return filepath.Join(sessionDir, stateFileName)
52	}
53	
54	// loadState reads session state, treating an absent or unparseable file as a
55	// fresh session.
56	//
57	// Corruption is deliberately non-fatal. The file exists only to suppress
58	// duplicate checkpoints; losing it costs at most one redundant checkpoint,
59	// whereas failing the hook would surface a warning in the user's aider session
60	// on every turn.
61	func loadState(sessionDir string) sessionState {
62		st := sessionState{LastTurnEnd: turnFingerprint{TurnIndex: -1}}
63		data, err := os.ReadFile(statePath(sessionDir))
64		if err != nil {
65			return st
66		}
67		// Unmarshal through a pointer, not a value. A file containing the literal
68		// `null` unmarshals successfully into a value and leaves it zeroed, which
69		// would report LastTurnEnd.TurnIndex == 0 — indistinguishable from "turn 0
70		// already checkpointed" — and silently swallow the first turn of the
71		// session. Into a pointer, `null` leaves it nil and is caught here.
72		var parsed *sessionState
73		if json.Unmarshal(data, &parsed) != nil || parsed == nil {
74			return st
75		}
76		return *parsed
77	}
78	
79	// saveState writes session state atomically.
80	func saveState(sessionDir string, st sessionState) error {
81		if err := os.MkdirAll(sessionDir, 0o750); err != nil {
82			return fmt.Errorf("create aider session dir: %w", err)
83		}
84		data, err := json.MarshalIndent(st, "", "  ")
85		if err != nil {
86			return fmt.Errorf("marshal aider session state: %w", err)
87		}
88		tmp := statePath(sessionDir) + ".tmp"
89		if err := os.WriteFile(tmp, data, 0o600); err != nil {
90			return fmt.Errorf("write aider session state: %w", err)
91		}
92		if err := os.Rename(tmp, statePath(sessionDir)); err != nil {
93			// Windows refuses a rename onto an open file; fall back to a direct
94			// write rather than losing the update.
95			_ = os.Remove(tmp)
96			if writeErr := os.WriteFile(statePath(sessionDir), data, 0o600); writeErr != nil {
97				return fmt.Errorf("write aider session state: %w", writeErr)
98			}
99		}
100		return nil
101	}
102	
103	// fingerprintOf summarizes the most recent turn. ok is false when the
104	// transcript holds no turns yet.
105	func fingerprintOf(turns []turn) (turnFingerprint, bool) {
106		if len(turns) == 0 {
107			return turnFingerprint{}, false
108		}
109		last := turns[len(turns)-1]
110		return turnFingerprint{
111			TurnIndex:   last.Index,
112			ReportCount: last.Usage.Reports,
113			EditCount:   len(last.ModifiedFiles),
114		}, true
115	}

test(aider): cover the aider adapter and fix a null state file

Adds unit tests for the four parts of the adapter that carry real risk:
hook install/uninstall against a user-owned .aider.conf.yml, turn-end
dedup, transcript parsing, and the protocol surface. 65 cases, 92.1%
statement coverage.

Fixes loadState: a state file holding the literal `null` unmarshalled
successfully into a zeroed struct, reporting TurnIndex == 0 -- which is
indistinguishable from "turn 0 already checkpointed" and would silently
swallow the first turn of a session. Unmarshalling through a pointer
catches it.

Adds BUILDATHON.md documenting the design decisions and their evidence
in aider's source.
